title: Ethiopian New Year Complete Feast
community: All of Ethiopia — Ethiopian New Year (September 11)
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian New Year Grand Feast — the complete Ethiopian New Year celebration: Doro Wat (ETH061), Key Wat (ETH021), Tibs (ETH022), Gomen (ETH106), Beyaynetu (ETH121), Enkutatash Cookies (ETH205), Honey Cake (ETH199), and Tej (ETH215). The most joyful feast in the Ethiopian calendar.
longDesc: Enkutatash (September 11 by the Gregorian calendar) is the Ethiopian New Year — celebrated when the rainy season ends, the yellow daisies bloom, and children carry flowers from house to house. The feast combines the best of Ethiopian meat cooking with the season's first harvest.
steps: 2 days before: Doro Wat, Key Wat, start Tej.
1 day before: bake cookies and cake.
New Year morning: assemble grand mesob. Open Tej.
chefTips: The yellow cookies (ETH205) are the visual centrepiece — yellow is the New Year colour.
commonMistakes: No yellow cookies — they are the seasonal signature.
sustainabilityTips: New Year food uses the first harvest — locally and seasonally sourced.
servedWith: Shared with neighbours and children carrying flowers
healthBenefits: New Year feast provides complete nutrition from every food group.
culturalNote: Enkutatash is Ethiopia's most joyful day — the end of the rains, the bloom of the yellow daisies, the children singing, and the families gathering to eat together. The Ethiopian New Year feast is the celebration of life, of harvest, and of community.
